newsitem.title: DENMARK: Red Cross vows action in Europe's health crisis.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross vows action in Europe's health crisis.

text.p: Representatives of 50 European Red Cross and Red Crescent groups called on Thursday for partnership in a major cross-border action plan to stave off an impending health crisis in post-Cold War eastern Europe.

"Europe is changing dramatically. It has more democracy than before but it has become less stable. It has more free markets but higher unemployment. There is less fear of an international war, yet the individual feels more insecure," the Red Cross and Red Crescent societies said in a declaration at the end of a four-day conference in Copenhagen.
The conference resulted in the signing of over 100 cooperation and partnership agreements between Red Cross and Red Crescent societies across Europe and the former Soviet Union.
Cross-continent partnership agreements were the key element in the declaration, which called for the humanitarian societies to work together to combat Europe's new wave of health hazards.

According to the Red Cross and Crescent common diseases such as diphtheria, typhoid and cholera have reappeared in eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union, where heart disease and suicide are growing in frequency and average male life expectancy fell from 65 years to 58 between 1989 and 1994.

"In many countries the health system has totally collapsed and the Red Cross has to fill the gaps. The national societies must find a joint strategy in the fight against the new Europe's diseases," acting Danish Red Cross president Freddy Karup Pedersen said.
"We must be ready to provide emergency aid but we must also hold governments to their duty to guarantee the health of citizens at national and international levels," he said.
"The demands on the Red Cross are getting bigger all the time, so this means we must work closer together, sharing each others' experience," Pedersen added.
Poverty is also a huge problem, with Red Cross estimates showing that over half the population of a former Soviet bloc country such as Bulgaria is living below the poverty line.

The conference brought together the international Red Cross and the Moslem Red Crescent organisations at national and international level, governmental and non-governmental as well as voluntary organisations and United Nations observers.
The Danish Red Cross hosted the meeting along with national societies in the rest of the Nordic region -- Norway, Sweden, Finland and Iceland.
It was the first time Red Cross and Crescent societies from both sides of Europe's old ideological divide had met since the Iron Curtain fell.

The post-communist period in eastern Europe has seen vast changes with war, growing ethnic tension, social polarisation, youth drug abuse, violence and new health and environmental problems aggravated by decreasing public resources placing an ever escalating responsibility on humanitarian organisations.
